params.name: ys
params.let: [k*m*i for i in [1,2,3,4]] if t == 0 else ([12*c//i for i in [1,2,3,4]] if t == 1 else [k*m*i + d for i in [1,2,3,4]])

params.name: concl
params.let: ['y/x is the same constant in every column, so it is a direct variation.', 'xy is the same constant in every column, so it is an inverse variation.', 'Neither y/x nor xy is constant, so it is neither a direct nor an inverse variation.']

stem: Decide whether the table represents a direct variation, an inverse variation or neither: $\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & {=xs[0]} & {=xs[1]} & {=xs[2]} & {=xs[3]} \\ \hline y & {=ys[0]} & {=ys[1]} & {=ys[2]} & {=ys[3]} \end{array}$

distractors.text: None of these can be decided from a table

notes: Neither case is y = kx + d (d>0), so neither xy nor y/x is constant. x values increasing, positive. Fourth distractor is a filler.
